page: Microsoft Azure E96as_v4 is a high-core-count, memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is driven by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at 3.525 GHz, providing 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. It is equipped with 672.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 7.0 GB per-vCPU ratio. Cache provisions include 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and a 32 MB L3 cache segment. For localized high-speed temporary operations, the instance bundles 1443 GB of local SSD storage, while omitting discrete GPU hardware.

Benchmark measurements indicate top-tier and strong throughput in parallelized compute and memory operations. In synthetic evaluations, the instance achieved a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 129815.6 and a PassMark encryption score of 103059.94, both landing within the top 10% tier. Multi-core performance is further emphasized by a Geekbench multi-core score of 18573.0, alongside strong results in Clang software compilation (50682.0) and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (459.91 GB/sec). Database capabilities show robust handling with PassMark database operations at 26160.75 and Redis reaching 89.47 million SET operations per second.

Conversely, single-threaded characteristics occupy middle-tier benchmark ranges, demonstrated by a Geekbench single-core score of 1658.0 and single-threaded gzip compression of 27.15 GB/sec. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth (134.24 GB/sec) and write bandwidth (65.08 GB/sec) also evaluate as average. From an efficiency perspective, the high vCPU and memory density provides favorable performance consolidation for scalable multithreaded systems, though workloads strictly constrained by per-core single-thread throughput or AVX-512 extensions will see limited utility due to AMD Zen 3 architectural attributes.

Given its massive memory allocation, 96 vCPUs, and 1443 GB local SSD, the E96as_v4 is structurally aligned with large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching solutions such as Redis, distributed data processing, and large continuous integration or build orchestration systems.
description: Microsoft Azure E96as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 96 dedicated vCPUs derived from 48 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 7763 processor clocked at 3.525 GHz. Configured with 672.0 GB of memory (7.0 GB per vCPU) and a bundled 1443 GB local SSD, this server targets heavy concurrent workloads without relying on dedicated GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier multi-threaded processing, notably in stress-ng multi-core (129815.6) and PassMark encryption (103059.94), paired with high Redis throughput at 89.47 million operations per second. However, single-core metrics and uncached large-block memory transfers register in average tiers. The platform provides strong qualitative compute density and memory consolidation, making it well suited for large relational databases, in-memory caches, software compilation clusters, and heavy multithreaded analytics pipelines.
